text.p: European semiconductor maker SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV said on Thursday it had been able to maintain gross margins and was capacity-constrained.
The company posted a 7.1 percent increase in third quarter earnings to $132.4 million from $129.0 million last year.

"We believe our results for the quarter set us apart from the industry average in this difficult market environment," president and chief executive office Pasquale Pistorio said in a statement with the results.

"As expected net revenues were lower on a sequential quarterly basis. However differentiated products continued to grow as a percentage of revenues reaching almost 60 percent in the third quarter," he added.
"Therefore, while we are experiencing pricing pressures of varying degrees throughout our product portfolio, we have been able, so far, to maintain reasonable gross margins.
"In fact, the company remains overall capacity-constrained in its leading-edge submicron products," Pistorio said.
